messages.content: Could you retrieve the current weather data for New York, specifically focusing on the temperature?.

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.reasoning:
We need to call the function `requests_get` with appropriate params.

Open-Meteo API requires lat/lon. For NYC approximate lat=40.7128, lon=-74.0060. We want temperature. Probably we can ask for "temperature_2m". So query param? According to open-meteo docs, we use "?latitude=&longitude=&hourly=temperature_2m&current_weather=true".

But our tool signature only includes certain fields: url, headers optional, timeout, params object containing latitude, longitude, elevation. It doesn't allow specifying other query parameters like hourly etc. But maybe we can pass them via params as part of dictionary? Wait the schema shows params has keys: latitude?, longitude?, elevation?. Only those three. No ability to specify variable list. That seems limited. Maybe they omitted others but still accept arbitrary additional ones? Not sure. Might not support retrieving temperature directly unless using current_weather which returns temp. In open-meteo, adding &current_weather=true will return JSON including temperature. But if we can't set that param, perhaps we cannot get temperature. However we could try passing extra param through params dict beyond defined keys - might ignore unknown keys. Could also embed into URL manually? The function expects full URL plus params separate. We could construct URL with all needed query strings ourselves. Eg: url="https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast", then add ?latitude=...&longitude=...&current_weather=true . Then leave params empty {}. That may work because the function uses given URL + params appended automatically? Usually requests.get(url=url, params=params...). So if we already encode query in URL, it's fine. We'll do that.

Thus:

URL: "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=40.7128&longitude=-74.0060&current_weather=true"

No params needed.

Let's produce function call.
